comparison: Both strongly support the core findings on caspase activation and selective Nup degradation (C2, C14, C36, C38-C40, C172-C173). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of immunoblotting data, while peer reviewers praise methodology as 'convincing and state-of-the-art' and 'superb quality.' OpenEval covers additional claims (C30-C34) about caspase activation kinetics that peer reviewers address separately in R8.

Both support the functional characterization of trimmed NPCs showing selective export impairment (C3, C15, C45, C47-C48, C52-C53, C64). Reviewer 3 specifically highlights 'specific inhibition of nuclear export' as a key finding. OpenEval notes complementary assays used; peer review includes C89 not in OpenEval's list but raises no concerns about the functional data.

Perfect agreement on proteomics findings (C4, C16, C55-C56, C59-C60, C92-C93, C95-C97, C102, C106, C110-C111, C147). Reviewer 3 specifically praises the 'quantitative proteomic analysis' as 'a highlight' and notes the important caspase inhibitor control. OpenEval notes lack of technical replicate information and incomplete quantification of synthesis vs. export contributions, issues not raised by peer reviewers.

Both support neurogenesis findings (C5, C19, C126-C128). OpenEval expresses concern about limited characterization compared to myogenesis data (single time course, no imaging/functional assays). Peer reviewers accept these data as part of demonstrating NPC trimming in 'muscle (and other) differentiation programs' without raising concerns about depth of characterization.

Both support ER stress findings (C6, C21, C130-C131, C137-C141). OpenEval notes XIAP explanation is correlative without direct manipulation and chronic stress experiment lacks functional characterization. Peer reviewers accept ER stress data without specific concerns, viewing it as part of broader demonstration of NPC trimming contexts.

Both support reversibility/selectivity of NPC trimming (C7, C144, C174). Reviewer 1 notes 'high substrate specificity' and Reviewer 3 emphasizes the 'new broadly impactful concept' that caspases can be productive rather than destructive. OpenEval notes that reversibility is shown only by Nup level recovery without direct functional measurements, a limitation not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Both support FAK-myogenin mechanistic connection (C17, C148-C151). Peer reviewers accept the 'mechanistic insights' without specific critique. OpenEval emphasizes the evidence is correlative and notes no experiment directly tests whether preventing NPC trimming blocks FAK function or whether FAK is sufficient when trimming is blocked.

Both support pharmacological experiments with leptomycin B and Q-VD-OPh (C66, C68-C69). Peer reviewers view these as establishing functional importance for myogenesis. OpenEval notes lack of dose-response characterization and ambiguity about whether Q-VD-OPh effects are due to blocking NPC trimming specifically or other caspase functions.

Both support calpain inhibitor findings (C42-C43) showing calpains are upstream of caspases but not directly responsible for NPC trimming. OpenEval notes experiment uses single concentration and timepoint without testing effects on extent versus timing. Peer reviewers accept this mechanistic detail without concerns.

Both support fragment dissociation heterogeneity (C70-C72, C74-C75, C87-C88). Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'fragments are sometimes associated with the NPCs.' OpenEval notes molecular mechanisms determining retention versus release are not investigated and functional significance remains unclear. Peer reviewers do not raise these mechanistic questions.

Both support preservation of Crm1 and importin localization (C78, C91). OpenEval includes C79 about 'subdued' export defect being speculative without direct rate comparisons. Peer reviewers accept these findings as consistent with selective peripheral Nup degradation and functional NPC characterization.

Partial overlap on temporal relationships. OpenEval R5 covers C114-C120, C122-C124 about myogenin timing and feedback regulation. Peer R8 addresses C30-C34, C114-C116 about caspase activation kinetics. Both support the temporal characterization; peer reviewers note 'NPC-related course of events' without specific concerns about timing data.

Partial overlap on import function during NPC trimming. OpenEval R5 includes C118-C120 about TprC⁻ Myog+ cells demonstrating import functions during trimming. Peer R11 accepts that 'nuclear import...remain[s] mostly functional' consistent with these observations. Both support this functional characterization.

Both support primary myoblast validation (C18, C121). OpenEval notes data limited to immunofluorescence at single timepoint without comprehensive C2C12 characterization. Peer reviewers accept primary cell data as supporting functional import during trimming without raising concerns about depth.

Both address integrated transcriptomics-proteomics analysis (C109, C112-C113). OpenEval supports the findings but notes relative contributions of synthesis/import/export/stability not quantitatively deconvolved. Peer R15 is UNCERTAIN, noting work 'fall[s] short in demonstrating that NPC trimming is actually required' for differentiation - a stronger critique about causality than OpenEval's technical concerns.

Both address generality claims (C20). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting two cell types insufficient to claim generality across differentiation. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the conceptual advance, with Reviewer 1 stating work will be 'of broad interest' and Reviewer 3 emphasizing 'broadly impactful concept.' Peer reviewers focus on conceptual contribution rather than empirical generality.

Partial overlap on conceptual framework (C164, C166). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting continuum between sublethal and lethal caspase functions requires experimental validation. Peer R14 SUPPORTS the conceptual advance about productive caspase functions. Peer reviewers emphasize novelty of concept; OpenEval emphasizes need for experimental validation.

Partial overlap on caspase activation timing (C30-C34). OpenEval R1 supports these claims as part of comprehensive immunoblotting data. Peer R8 accepts temporal characterization as part of 'NPC-related course of events.' Both support the timing data without concerns.

OpenEval supports pathway inhibitor experiments (C167, C169-C171) mapping NPC trimming relative to known differentiation pathways, noting single inhibitor limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address these pathway positioning experiments.

OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN the hypothesis about NPC-genome organization effects (C157-C161), noting lack of chromatin conformation analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address this speculative hypothesis about genome organization.

OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN the functional interpretations of ER stress data (C162-C163), noting lack of protein synthesis, ER load, or homeostasis measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers accept ER stress observations without addressing these specific functional claims.

OpenEval supports nuclear accumulation of specific protein classes (C154-C156) but notes functional significance not tested and connections to DNA damage/mitochondrial communication are correlative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address these protein class observations.

OpenEval supports RNA-seq data showing peripheral Nup loss is proteolytic not transcriptional (C175-C176), but notes lack of statistical analysis and error bars. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address this mechanistic distinction.

OpenEval supports RNA FISH findings (C49-C51) but notes C51 about housekeeping RNA buffering is speculative without direct synthesis rate measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address RNA stability and homeostasis claims.

OpenEval supports proximity ligation assay data (C62-C63) showing focal adhesion protein interactions but notes lack of quantification and functional testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers do not specifically address PLA experiments.
